newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 21.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

A leaked Federal Government briefing paper claims Malaysian logging interests helped bring about the downfall of the Solomon Islands Government in 1994. The document has already brought angry reactions from South Pacific nations, whose leaders and economies the document criticises. Page 1.

Macquarie Underwriting estimates that this financial year seems certain to be the biggest for equity raisings in Australia's history, with investors expected to be asked for at least A$23 billion to equity issues in 1997-98. The biggest float should be that of Telstra, expected to raise up to A$10 billion. Page 1.

Market economists have predicted the June quarter consumer price index, to be released this week by the Australian Bureau of Statistics, will show Australia's underlying interest rate has fallen below the Reserve Bank's target of two to three per cent, signallig a possible further cut in interest rates. Page 3.

The Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union last night indicated it was still prepared to negotiate with Rio Tinto despite subsidiary Coal & Allied's decision to freight coal through a picket line tomorrow. The union said the freight attempt wouldfail, and will respond to the company's enterprise bargaining demands before the Australian Industrial Relations Commission today. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Three army officers involved in the crash of two Black Hawk helicopters last year are facing courts martial. Army Land Commander Major-General Frank Hickling has recommended disciplinary charges be laid against the officers in relation to their responsibiities for the safety of the mission which claimed the lives of 15 soldiers and three aircrew. Page 1.

The recommendations of an inquiry into teacher training, to be put to Federal Schools Minister David Kemp next month, include the outside review of teacher training courses in order to establish quality control over the 10,000 annual teaching graduates eah year. The Victorian Government yesterday announced its own review of graduate quality. Page 1.

Over the past six years, the two main television networks, Seven and Nine, have together lost 280,000 viewers from their weeknight six o'clock news ratings, perplexing industry executives. Industry participants have cited the introduction of flexitime, woking from home, high unemployment, pay-TV, and a shift to other networks or late night news for the falling figures. Page 1.

The Mapping the Future report on the national anti-drug effort has recommended State and Federal Ministers spend more on the fight against drugs after it was found that just over two percent of the A$7 billion in taxes collected on alcohol and tobacco was pent on drug-use research, treatment and prevention. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

An AC Nielsen-McNair survey of 200 Asian business leaders found 16 per cent of those who were aware of Independent MP Pauline Hanson were less likely to do business with Australia because of statements made by her. Twenty-one per cent said they were less likely to travel to Australia, with many calling Hanson a racist and anti-Asian. Page 1.

The Federal Government has instructed all Australian Pacific heads of missions that a confidential briefing paper made public on the weekend did not reflect official policy or views. The document, which attacks many regional politicians as corrupt, was baed on the views of Government experts on the South Pacific. Page 1.

Over the past year in New South Wales, there have been five magistrates' statements accusing police of colluding on evidence, telling lies under oath, making up statements or not being objective as witnesses, despite these practices being exposed by the Wood Royal Commission. Page 1.

Queensland University researcher Professor Mat Darveniza has survived a lightning strike of a million volts by using a portable protector device which consists of three aluminium pipes joined together to create a triangular frame large enough for a personto stand under it. Page 3.
THE AGE

The Victorian Government has ordered a review into teacher training methods with Education Minister Phil Gude expressing concern over evidence some universities were producing poor quality teaching graduates who were ill-prepared for the school system. Pae 1.

A secret report by the Office of National Assessments said New Zealand spoils Australia's foreign policy in an effort to disguise the nation's increasing degree of economic and defence dependence on Canberra. The report also said New Zealand ministers have undercut Australia's attempts to stop logging in the Solomon Islands. Page 1.

For over six weeks anti-logging protesters have been engaged in non-violent but sometimes dangerous sabotages to slow logging in the Goolengook forest in the East Gippsland wilderness of Victoria. The protestors use thumb locks and steel pipes to lock theselves on to tractors and sometimes police have to use angle-grinders to cut them free. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday announced he had appointed a taskforce of Australian bureaucrats to continue international lobbying for the Federal Government's greenhouse gas reduction policy. The taskforce will follow up on Howard's discussions on limate change with the United States, Japanese and British Governments. Page A2.
-- Reuters Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
